title: Rhiannon (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Produced by Keith Olsen; "it was one of those songs that took over a day to get the basic track". Personnel: Mick Fleetwood, drums. Live, 1975-82, the song "took on a theatrical intensity".

title: Mick Fleetwood (Patrick Berkery, Modern Drummer, 23 April 2009)
notes: Read through a summarising fetch. "The hollowed-out verses of The Chain, the delicate brushwork of Sara, and the steady pulse of Dreams"; "his penchant for playing patterns of accents where you least expect them" (Gold Dust Woman); he rarely repeats a figure when a section returns. Fleetwood: "With me, it's back-to-front sometimes"; "I play very physically"; "I pride myself on time"; "John and I play like blues players, really"; "the approach John and I have was learned in the trenches playing with Sonny Boy Williamson"; "I'm not Gene Krupa"; no lessons, "training on the job", a toy kit called a Gigster. Admires Phil Seamen and Micky Waller ("great feel drummer"); compared with Jim Keltner.

title: Listen to the isolated drums on Fleetwood Mac song 'Go Your Own Way' (Tyler Golsen, Far Out, 9 April 2022)
notes: "Fleetwood rarely plays the same pattern twice in a row"; "stays on the beat the entire way"; the snare on 2 and 4 only in the choruses, the verses "tom-heavy". Quotes Ken Caillat: "For some reason, when he played his hi-hat, it distracted him."
